A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ReSplat study, with complete main text, references, and Appendices A-C. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, and figures across all 26 pages.

before.justification: v3 reports original view-synthesis experiments, reconstruction timings, generalization tests, and architectural ablations in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and additionally reports an AnySplat comparison and a brief per-attribute update analysis.

M1.justification: The compact initialization, rendering-error feedback, recurrent updates, training objectives, and local kNN alternative are retained. The per-attribute observation does not change the update procedure, and streaming is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DL3DV, RealEstate10K, and ACID with the same view-count, resolution, and generalization scenarios. The added AnySplat comparison does not introduce new dataset or task coverage; streaming is not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds AnySplat to the single-step versus recurrent comparison, retaining WorldMirror and the ReSplat variants. SplatFormer remains evaluated: its comparison moves from v3 Appendix A and Table S3 into v4 Section 4.1.

E3.justification: The stated splits, view counts, resolutions, metrics, training budgets, and ReSplat configurations are unchanged, including the 140-scene DL3DV evaluation. The additions specify no distinct new evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a brief 'Per-Attribute Update' analysis identifying which Gaussian attributes the recurrent module changes most. It reports predominant updates to centers, scales, and base colors, with negligible higher-order spherical-harmonic adjustments, but supplies no quantitative breakdown. Existing ablations and robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The existing practice of reporting individual metric values and curves remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 newly reports AnySplat at 20.79 PSNR, 0.643 SSIM, and 0.241 LPIPS. Appendix A adds the qualitative per-attribute finding. Matched prior numerical results remain unchanged, including all SplatFormer comparison values now reproduced in main-text prose.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(11), mathematical definitions, and the global/local kNN complexity arguments are retained. Equation-spacing and prose corrections do not alter mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about gradient-free recurrent refinement, compact Gaussian reconstruction, efficiency, and generalization. The new comparison supports the existing parameter-efficiency argument without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds a hypothesis that early iterations extract the most informative rendering-error signals, followed by diminishing returns. It also explicitly identifies the static-view-set limitation and discusses a possible sliding-window extension. v3 already acknowledged fixed Gaussian counts and saturation after four iterations.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information in Section 4 and Appendix B is retained, including attention settings, local-search radii, optimizer, training schedules, GH200 hardware, and code/pretrained-model access statements. SplatFormer normalization and grid-search details are moved into the main text.

R1.justification: The same 64 references and substantive distinctions from prior methods are retained. AnySplat was already cited in v3; its new experimental row does not revise the broader research positioning. The SplatFormer discussion is relocated rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: v4 corrects several grammatical errors, updates affiliations and acknowledgments, and moves the SplatFormer discussion into Section 4.1. Several specific appendix cross-references become generic references. These are limited edits within the retained overall section structure.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains an AnySplat row and revised caption. v3 Table S3 is replaced by numerical prose in the main text, with subsequent appendix tables renumbered and repositioned. Figures S1 and S2 shift vertically, while their images and the other figure content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional AnySplat comparison and explicit applicability limits modestly improve evaluation completeness and interpretation. Moving the retained SplatFormer evidence into Section 4.1 makes it more prominent, although replacing its table with prose and removing specific appendix references reduces scanability. The per-attribute addition lacks quantitative support, so the overall evidential gain remains limited.
